claims.statement: ArDoCo REST builds as io.github.ardoco:rest:2.1.0-SNAPSHOT on the io.github.ardoco:parent:2.2.0-SNAPSHOT parent POM; Spring Boot is managed by importing the spring-boot-dependencies 4.1.2 BOM into dependencyManagement, and the spring-boot-maven-plugin repackages the executable jar with main class edu.kit.kastel.mcse.ardoco.tlr.rest.ArDoCoRestApplication while the Failsafe plugin binds integration-test and verify to the integration-test phase.

The four ArDoCo libraries (io.github.ardoco.core:common, io.github.ardoco.id:pipeline-id, io.github.ardoco.tlr:pipeline-tlr, io.github.ardoco.tlr:text-preprocessing) resolve at the inherited ${ardoco.version} snapshot property from the parent POM; to make those snapshots resolvable, the pom declares Maven Central plus two snapshot-only repositories (releases disabled): the Sonatype maven-snapshots repository and ardocoSnapshots, the public read-only ARDoCo GitLab group packages mirror on gitlab.kit.edu that enables resolving the ARDoCo 2.2.0-SNAPSHOT builds from the Jackson 3 migration.

application.properties defines the operational knobs: Redis at 127.0.0.1:6379 with empty username/password, redis.time-to-live.hours=24, tlr.timeout.seconds=60, spring.servlet.multipart.max-file-size=200MB, management.endpoint.health.show-details=always, and management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=health (only the health actuator endpoint is exposed).

The Spring profile split differentiates deployment topologies: the docker profile sets spring.data.redis.host=redis for containers while the default and local profiles keep 127.0.0.1, and the local profile additionally widens cors.allowed-origins with localhost origins (http://localhost:3000, http://localhost:8000); the docker profile is activated by the Dockerfile's ENV SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=docker and by the CI job's SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=docker env var.

The documented local run flow is: fill credentials into redis/redis_template.env and rename it to redis/redis.env, start the infrastructure with docker-compose up -d from a compose file instantiated from docker-compose-template.yaml, start the application, use Swagger UI at localhost:8080, and inspect data at localhost:5540 (docker-compose down stops it; redis-cli access via docker exec -it redis redis-cli plus AUTH). The instantiated docker-compose.yml, redis.env, redis.conf, redis.acl, .env, data/*, and redisinsight/* are all gitignored, and because the template only exposes 6379 inside the compose network, a host-run application using the default profile cannot reach the containerized Redis without publishing the port.

docker-compose-template.yaml defines three restart:always services on the app-network bridge: redis (redis-server --bind 0.0.0.0 --port 6379, volume ./data:/data, port 6379 only exposed internally), redisinsight (redis/redisinsight published at 127.0.0.1:5540:5540, depends_on redis, volume ./redisinsight:/data), and app (built from the Dockerfile as ghcr.io/ardoco/rest, container ardoco-rest-api, published at 127.0.0.1:8080:8080, depends_on redis).

The two-stage Dockerfile builds with mvn -Daether.remoteRepositoryFilter.prefixes=true -Daether.remoteRepositoryFilter.prefixes.basedir=/build/.mvn/rrf -DskipTests clean package on maven:3-eclipse-temurin-25-alpine, using the checked-in .mvn/rrf/prefixes-mavenSnapshot.txt (a Maven Resolver remote-repository prefix filter whose only entry /org/springframework restricts the Sonatype snapshot repository to Spring artifacts), then runs the copied target/rest-*.jar on eclipse-temurin:25-jre-alpine with EXPOSE 8080, ENV SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=docker, and the entrypoint java -jar /app.jar --server.use-forward-headers=true --server.forward-headers-strategy=framework so the container honors forwarded headers behind a reverse proxy; CI instead verifies on Java 21 (Temurin).

.github/workflows/docker.yml publishes the container image by delegating to the reusable workflow ardoco/actions/.github/workflows/docker.yml@main with image-name rest and push true; it triggers on workflow_dispatch, on a monthly schedule (cron "17 4 25 * *") that rebuilds the image so its floating eclipse-temurin:25 base tags pick up JDK patches, on pushes to main ignoring **.md and .github/** paths, and on v* tags.

ci.yml runs mvn verify on ubuntu-latest with Temurin Java 21, SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=docker, and a redis service container published on 6379, on pushes and PRs to main plus manual dispatch; the Redis-backed tests do not rely on that service container because they provision their own Testcontainers Redis and override spring.data.redis.host/port dynamically (e.g. RedisAccessorTest).

openwiki.yml refreshes this wiki weekly Monday 06:00 UTC (cron 0 6 * * 1) or on manual dispatch; it grants contents:write and pull-requests:write and delegates entirely to the reusable workflow ardoco/actions/.github/workflows/openwiki.yml@main, passing the OPENROUTER_API_KEY secret, so the update logic is not inline.

The observable endpoints are: Swagger UI at /swagger-ui/index.html, the OpenAPI spec at /v3/api-docs, Spring Actuator health at /actuator/health with show-details=always, the HomeController redirect of / to Swagger UI, the lightweight /api/health returning a static OK (it does not verify the Redis connection), /api/configuration serving ArDoCo's default configuration as a map usable as additionalConfigs, and RedisInsight at http://localhost:5540.

The five runner families each expose /start and /start-and-wait under their base path (/api/ardocode, /api/arcotl, /api/swattr, /api/transarc, /api/find-inconsistencies), and cross-family result retrieval is available via /api/get-result/{id} and /api/wait-for-result/{id}.

At runtime /start answers HTTP 200 immediately with either a cached result or the requestId and a being-processed message; /start-and-wait and /api/wait-for-result/{id} block up to tlr.timeout.seconds (60s) and return 200 with the result or 202 when the wait times out; /api/get-result/{id} returns 202 while the pipeline is in flight; results expire from Redis after redis.time-to-live.hours (24h) so a repeated request re-runs the pipeline; and a failed pipeline stores an "Error: "-prefixed message under the request ID with the same TTL so a retry within the window surfaces the cached failure.

The global exception handler maps FileNotFoundException, FileConversionException, and IllegalArgumentException to HTTP 422, TimeoutException to 408, and ArdocoException (pipeline failures and cached error values) to 500, with a general Exception fallback to 500.

The pom adds two test-scope Spring Boot artifacts — spring-boot-restclient and spring-boot-resttestclient — alongside spring-boot-starter-test, and the controller integration tests use them: AbstractTLRControllerTest imports TestRestTemplate from org.springframework.boot.resttestclient and drives its HTTP calls with it.

The pom declares the Jedis client (redis.clients:jedis, compile scope, currently 8.0.2), but no Java source or test references it — the runtime Redis path is Spring Data Redis over Lettuce via the LettuceConnectionFactory and RedisTemplate beans in ApplicationConfig. The declaration is dead weight and must not be mistaken for the active persistence client.

CORS for browser clients is configured via cors.allowed-origins in application.properties (default https://ardoco.de, comma-separated, empty disables CORS, overridable via the CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS environment variable through Spring relaxed binding); WebConfig applies it as a single CORS mapping on /api/** with allowed methods GET and POST and allowCredentials(false), the local profile extends the list with localhost origins, and WebConfigCorsTest pins the semantics (allowed-origin preflight accepted with GET,POST and no credentials header, foreign origin and DELETE preflight rejected 403, empty list yields no CORS headers).

Dependency automation is Renovate-based: renovate.json extends the shared preset local>ArDoCo/actions:renovate-preset (so cadence and most behavior live in the preset, not in this repository) and its only explicit package rule disables org.junit.jupiter:** with the description "JUnit is aligned manually with the version managed by Spring Boot (junit.version in pom.xml)", matching the pinned ${junit.version} (6.0.3) and the explicit junit-jupiter-api, junit-jupiter-engine, and junit-jupiter-params declarations that make the override effective; the repository carries no Dependabot configuration and no repository-level rule automates the eclipse-temurin/maven base images, so the JDK line is manually managed on LTS (Java 25 in the image, 21 in CI).
